title: Gradient by number

reference.source: Antonin Waterkeyn (@antonin.work), shown in a Nodi post; frames read from the 576 × 716 stream
reference.grammar: a letterform rasterized to square cells on white graph paper; each inked cell flat-filled in one of five inks (red, blue-violet, pink, yellow, dark green) with one digit 1–8 centered in it; the black grid runs over everything

units: plate widths; the plate is 1 wide and 1.243 tall, y down

grid.line: #0a0a0b at 75 % alpha, max(1 px, w/700), drawn after the fills

glyph.depth: max(0, 1 − d / half_width), d = distance to the centerline

light.m: 1 − smoothstep(0.26, 0.74, r), r squeezed 0.70 across the light direction

techniques.name: Graph paper
techniques.implementation: White fill; the grid is stroked after every cell so the fills never cover it, which is the one thing that makes the cells read as paper squares instead of pixels.

techniques.name: Cell inking

params.offsets: center and ±0.3 cell on both diagonals
params.rule: center counts 2; ink when the sum reaches 3

techniques.implementation: Five depth samples per cell vote on whether the cell is inside the stroke, so a thin pass through a cell corner does not ink it and a cell straddling the edge does.

techniques.name: Depth field under a light
techniques.implementation: One scalar per cell: how deep the cell center sits in the stroke, scaled by the same elliptical light field as ST-09, so the right side of the 9 runs to the top of the ramp and the left stays low.

techniques.name: Quantize to a digit

params.ink: #3e4027 when the cell’s OKLab L > 0.55, else L + 0.42

techniques.implementation: The digit is the level index. It is drawn after the fill in a single ink read from the reference, lifted only on the dark green cells where it would vanish.

techniques.name: Per-cell gradient on the slope

params.direction: ∇f from the four neighbors, empty neighbors read 0
params.fallback: flat ramp((k − 0.5)/9) when the slope is zero

techniques.implementation: A linear gradient across the cell from the low side to the high side of its level; the direction is the discrete gradient of f, so neighboring cells chain into a continuous ramp while each one stays a square.

techniques.name: Five inks, one ramp
techniques.implementation: The reference’s five flat inks, in the order they occur from the edge of a stroke to its spine, become stops of a continuous OKLab ramp; level 1 sits at the first stop and level 9 at the last.

pass_order: per cell: gradient fill, then digit
coupling: f alone decides which cells ink, the digit, both fill colors and the fill direction, so a digit can never disagree with its color.
inferred: how the source assigns digits (they vary inside one color band)
the reference’s tool; the fills there are flat
departure: The reference fills each cell flat and its digits do not read as a measurement. Here the fill slopes and the digit measures it; that is the technique this plate adds.
notes: Seedless; the render is deterministic for a given light position.
A typed glyph is rasterized in Geist 600 and read through an exact Euclidean distance transform; the inking, the digits and the fills follow.
